title: Sales enablement: positioning & messaging, competitive briefs, pitch deck guidance, pricing, case studies, security FAQ
author: Arielle Chen
summary: Comprehensive sales enablement playbook for Redwood Inference covering core positioning and messaging for buyer personas, competitive brief summaries and rebuttals, suggested pitch deck structure and metrics, pricing guidance and examples, representative case studies, and a prospect-facing security FAQ. This doc is the canonical reference for AEs and SDRs when engaging technical buyers and GTM partners.
audience: Account executives, solutions engineers, SDRs, GTM enablement, partner reps, sales leadership
positioning_and_messaging:
Overview:
Redwood Inference is the developer-first inference platform that makes production LLM serving predictable, economical, and reliable across hosted, dedicated, and private deployment modes. Core value propositions:
- Production-first performance: low-latency, high-throughput serving runtime tuned for real product traffic patterns (continuous batching, KV/prefix cache, quantization profiles).
- Unified runtime across environments: same API, rollouts, and observability for hosted API, Dedicated reserved pools, and Private (VPC/on-prem) deployments.
- Cost-aware controls: measurable levers (batching, caching, quantization, routing policies) that reduce per-token unit economics while preserving output quality.
- Reliability & graceful degradation: automated model fallback, region routing, and canary rollouts to protect SLAs.
Buyer persona messaging (short talking points):
- Product/ML Engineer (technical): "Ship with predictable latency and throughput — same API across prod, dedicated, and private environments. We'll help you optimize tail latency and cost without rewriting your stack."
- Platform/Infra Team: "Standardize inference across business units with observability, RBAC, and rollout tooling. Dedicated capacity and private deployments meet isolation and compliance requirements."
- CTO / VP Eng (economic): "Lower per-feature cost through batching/caching recommendations and reserved capacity while maintaining quality SLAs; shorten time-to-value with our hosted API and clear migration path to Dedicated/Private."
- Security/Compliance Lead: "Private deployment options, KMS/HSM integrations, audit logging, and SOC/ISO evidence packages to meet regulatory requirements."
One-line elevator pitch:
"Redwood Inference gives engineering teams a single, predictable runtime to serve LLMs at production scale — fast to start (hosted), predictable at scale (Dedicated), and secure for regulated workloads (Private)."
competitive_briefs:
Summary of top competitors and concise battlecards:
1) Hyperscaler-managed endpoints (e.g., CloudX AI Endpoints)
- Strengths: deep cloud integration, single-provider convenience, strong global infra.
- Weaknesses / Redwood counters: less optimized for inference economics; limited model/quantization guidance; vendor lock-in concerns.
- Key rebuttals: Redwood provides model-aware kernel selection and quantization profiles that reduce per-token cost; our Dedicated and Private options avoid lock-in and support multi-cloud strategies.
2) LLM API pure-play providers (e.g., API-First Models Inc.)
- Strengths: frictionless API and fast experimentation.
- Weaknesses / Redwood counters: may prioritize simplicity over production SLOs and observability.
- Key rebuttals: emphasize Redwood’s production tooling (tracing, per-route latency/cost breakdowns) and rollout controls that matter to engineering teams.
3) Self-hosted inference vendors / open-source stacks (e.g., InferenceStack OSS)
- Strengths: full control, low licensing cost.
- Weaknesses / Redwood counters: operational burden and hidden TCO.
- Key rebuttals: Redwood offers a managed control plane for Private deployments and on-prem packaging plus runbooks and support to reduce ops burden; present TCO comparison with 12–24 month horizon.
Battlecard quick points (tech objections and responses):
- "We can self-host cheaper": Share TCO worksheet: include engineering hours, infra ops, model tuning, and reliability overhead vs Redwood’s managed features and reserved capacity economics.
- "We need on-prem": Redwood Private supports air-gapped on-prem installs and customer-managed networking; provide reference architecture and support cadence.
- "We need specific model versions / quant": Highlight model catalog, verifiable performance profiles, and quantization recommendations by workload with examples (INT8/4bit profiles and expected throughput gains).
Competitive collateral to share: one-pager TCO, sample benchmark results for common workloads (chat QPS vs cost), and a reference architecture diagram for private deployment.
pitch_deck_guidance:
Recommended slide flow (15–18 slides):
1. Title & customer hook (1 slide) – specific pain: e.g., "Why inference is your new SRE problem"
2. Problem framed with metrics (1 slide) – latency tail, cost per token, variance in throughput across models
3. Market context & why now (1 slide)
4. What Redwood solves (1 slide) – three pillars: performance, cost, control
5. Product demo snapshot (1 slide) – API example, streaming response, function/tool calling
6. Deployment modes (1 slide) – Hosted, Dedicated, Private with short bullets and ideal use-cases
7. Architecture (1–2 slides) – serving runtime, kernel selection, caching, routing policies (simple diagram)
8. Observability & ops (1 slide) – Console metrics, per-route cost, tracing hooks
9. Pricing & economics (1 slide) – sample pricing tiers and reserved commit example
10. Case studies (2 slides) – short customer outcomes with metrics (latency reduction, cost savings)
11. Security & compliance (1 slide) – KMS/HSM, audit logs, SOC/ISO evidence status
12. Rollout plan & migration path (1 slide) – PoC -> Pilot -> Production (owner, timeline)
13. Success metrics & SLAs (1 slide) – expected SLOs, support levels, escalation path
14. Pricing & next steps (1 slide) – E2E pricing example, trial offer, contact
15. Appendix / technical Q&A (1–3 slides)
Pitch best practices:
- Always include a one-slide TCO example tailored to the prospect (estimate tokens/day, average seq length, batch size assumptions).
- Include an ops playbook slide for technical buyers: expected infra changes, integration steps, and SSO/KMS checklist.
- For enterprise prospects, include a migration diagram from hosted -> dedicated -> private and a sample SLA table.
Required metrics to include in demo: tail latency p95/p99, tokens/sec, per-token cost estimate, and throughput at different sequence lengths.
Slide assets available in the GTM assets repo: benchmark charts, architecture SVGs, customer logos with reference quotes (legal-approved list).
pricing_guidance:
High-level pricing guidance (for prospect conversations):
- Hosted API: usage-based pricing (per-token generation + per-embedding unit). Typical entry pricing example: $0.0008 / input token, $0.002 / output token (example rates; use legal-approved price sheet). Free-tier credits available for PoC.
- Dedicated: reserved capacity with monthly or annual commit. Example offering: predictable $/hour per GPU equivalent with included baseline throughput, optional burst capacity. Discount tiers apply at 6/12/24-month commits.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): platform license + optional support retainer. Pricing factors: number of nodes/GPU, required retention of audit logs, support SLAs, and optional on-site professional services.
Guidance for deal structuring:
- Use PoC credits and a 3-month Pilot with defined success criteria (throughput, latency, cost targets). If success, propose a 12-month Dedicated commit with scale checkpoints.
- For mid-market deals, lead with Hosted for quick time-to-value; propose Dedicated when estimate shows >30% cost savings or predictable demand.
- For regulated customers, price Private as license + support; coordinate with legal for data residency and SOC evidence requests.
Discounting and approvals:
- Standard discount band: up to 15% allowed by AE; >15% requires sales leadership and finance approval. Dedicated multi-year >25% requires VP sign-off. Always attach a short TCO model to justify discount.
Example cost worksheet inputs to use during discovery (share as template): average tokens/day, p95/p99 latency targets, acceptable max cost per 1k tokens, retention and logging needs, model families in scope.
case_studies:
Customer: NovaDocs (document automation SaaS)
- Problem: unpredictable latency during peak ingestion windows and high per-document inference cost.
- Solution: migrated to Redwood Dedicated with prefix KV caching and model quantization profiles; implemented automatic batching for batched summarization workflows.
- Outcome: 55% reduction in per-document inference cost, p99 latency improved from 2.8s to 0.9s, and predictable monthly spend enabling a pricing change that increased margins by 8 points.
Customer: ShopSmart (e-commerce personalization)
- Problem: inconsistent serving performance across regions and difficulty scaling during promotional events.
- Solution: used Redwood smart routing (region + cost policy) and reserved Dedicated pools in two regions, with Canary rollouts for new model versions.
- Outcome: 99.95% uptime during peak events, improved add-to-cart conversion by 2.4% attributable to lower latency and better personalization quality; estimated incremental revenue of $120k/quarter.
How to use case studies: always include metrics, team contact (if referenceable), and a short technical appendix with architecture and config used (batch sizes, sequence length assumptions, quantization profile).
security_faq:
Prospect security FAQ (short answers for RFP and initial prospect conversations):
Q1: Where is customer data stored and processed?
A1: For Hosted API, data is processed in region-selected Redwood-managed compute; logs and retention are configurable per-customer. For Dedicated and Private, data processing occurs in customer-dedicated capacity or customer-managed infrastructure (VPC/on-prem).
Q2: Do you support customer-managed encryption keys (KMS/HSM)?
A2: Yes. We integrate with major cloud KMS providers and support HSM-based key management for Private deployments.
Q3: What audit and logging capabilities exist?
A3: The Console provides request-level audit logs, model version metadata, and admin activity logs. We support export to SIEMs via secure forwarders and configurable retention windows.
Q4: What compliance evidence is available?
A4: Redwood maintains SOC2 Type II and is ISO 27001 aligned; we can provide controls mapping and evidence packages under NDA. Private deployments can be validated with on-site audits per contract.
Q5: How do you handle data residency requirements?
A5: Hosted customers may choose region-specific processing where available. Dedicated/private deployments enable strict data residency and on-prem options for regulated workloads.
Q6: How do you secure the inference runtime?
A6: Multi-layer security: hardened base images, network segmentation, RBAC for control plane, signed model artifacts, and per-token request authentication. We employ runtime scanning and periodic penetration tests.
Q7: What is your incident response and escalation process?
A7: We provide a published incident response process for customers with SLAs: designated severity levels, on-call rotations, timed escalations, and post-incident reports with root cause analysis. Dedicated/Private customers have a prioritized response channel.
Q8: Do you retain request payloads or model outputs?
A8: Retention is configurable per-account. By default, Hosted collects short-term logs for debugging; we offer options for no retention for sensitive workloads and can accommodate contract-level data deletion policies.
Suggested collateral to attach to RFPs: SOC2 summary, network architecture for Private, sample SLA, and legal-approved security one-pager.
next_steps_and_playbook:
PoC / Pilot playbook (technical + commercial steps):
1. Discovery (Week 0–1): collect tokens/day, seq length distribution, target latency SLOs, retention requirements, and models in scope.
2. PoC setup (Week 1–2): provision sandbox Hosted account or short Dedicated trial; deploy sample workload; configure metrics export and logging.
3. Measurement (Week 2–4): run representative traffic; collect p95/p99 latency, throughput, and per-token cost.
4. Optimize (Week 4–6): apply quantization suggestions, caching, and batching; rerun benchmarks.
5. Pilot review (Week 6): present results, TCO model, and recommended next steps (Dedicated/Private).
6. Contracting & Rollout (Month 2–3): finalize commit, migration plan, and support SLAs.
Ownership matrix:
- AE: commercial lead, contract approvals, customer success alignment
- SE: technical lead for PoC, integration steps, and runbook handoff
- Customer Success: onboarding, runbook reviews, performance monitoring during ramp
- Legal/Finance: contracting and discount approvals
Playbook assets: PoC checklist, data collection template (tokens/day sample), TCO worksheet, and technical runbook for SSO/KMS integration.
